messages:
maria: FYI customer AcmeCorp opened an escalation — their Private control plane agents started failing TLS handshakes to our control plane after a network appliance firmware upgrade.
maria: Errors in their logs: "TLS handshake failed: unexpected_message" and our control-plane logs show EOF during handshake.
josh: Do they have packet captures or openssl output? that usually narrows it down.
maria: They attached an openssl s_client run from a host in the VPC. i pasted the relevant bit below.
maria: ```
$ openssl s_client -connect cp.redwood.example.com:443 -alpn h2 -servername cp.redwood.example.com
CONNECTED(00000003)
140735208123456:error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure:ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:1529:
---
No ALPN negotiated
---
```
maria: note the client requests ALPN h2 but server negotiation shows "No ALPN negotiated".
irene: hmm. ALPN being stripped or rewritten strongly points to a TLS-inspecting proxy on egress. Many proxies terminate TLS or remove ALPN when doing downstream inspection.
josh: agreed. if the customer's egress appliance is doing TLS termination or active inspection it may be doing a re-enc of the upstream connection with a different ALPN or none. for mTLS to our control plane we require ALPN (http/1.1 or h2 depending on agent), and certificate passthrough for client cert validation.
maria: customer says they upgraded a firewall/ssl-inspection module last night to 12.4.4 and flipped on "deep ssl inspection" by default.
irene: ask them to try two quick checks: 1) curl with --http2 -v to our host from an affected host and 2) a tcpdump of the ClientHello to see if ALPN extension is present on the wire. if ClientHello on the wire already lacks ALPN, it's an agent issue; if it has ALPN but server sees none, middlebox is mutating it.
maria: they ran tcpdump and attached hex dump — the ClientHello ALPN bytes are present on the host -> wire. but when we look at our front-end tcpdump, the ALPN bytes are missing.
josh: that's definitive: the appliance is modifying the TLS handshake. tell them to exempt our control-plane IPs from interception (TLS passthrough) or configure "forward TLS" for those destinations. if they cannot exempt, they must use an egress NAT that keeps original TLS intact.
maria: i shared that and suggested a temporary workaround: have them add the control plane FQDN to their "do not inspect" list. they asked if there's a specific IP range to allow — i gave them our control plane IP CIDR: 34.212.120.0/22 and 3.125.44.0/23 (example ranges) and requested SNI bypass if IP allowlists not supported.
irene: also confirm that their device isn't downgrading cipher suites or doing RSA key exchange only — our mTLS requires ECDHE so Kx changes can also break handshake.
josh: i've created internal ticket ENG-NET-4729 and pinged eng-infra oncall to watch for retries/alerts. please paste any capture links in the ticket.
sre-bot: Reminder: if customer enables TLS passthrough, ensure they do not also strip client cert headers — mTLS validation requires the original client cert chain.
maria: Customer applied SNI bypass rule for cp.redwood.example.com and reports agent updates now connect successfully. they also rolled back the deep-inspection feature as a test and that fixed it too.
maria: they confirmed no more handshake_errors in their logs and control plane shows successful client cert auth.
josh: great. closing as configuration change on their side. will keep ENG-NET-4729 open for a bit in case of recurrence and to gather firmware/version notes.
irene: add note to KB: "Egress TLS inspection can strip ALPN/SNI causing mTLS handshake failures with Redwood Private control plane" and include recommended allowlist rules and example tcpdump checks.
maria: thanks team :thumbsup: customer happy, sent them COA and KB link.
